races.name: John Ormonde Wexford Sand Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
Newtownanner Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ballyskeagh
runners_data.note: OR=120 front-runner trained by Joseph O'Brien, last won over 7f on Good and steps up to a mile here; two-from-two on similar going is a strong platform and Chris Hayes knows this filly's habits, but she faces two rivals equally intent on leading and the question is whether she can dominate rather than simply compete for the front.|
runners_data.comment: Ballyskeagh won last time out but was fifth two starts back, giving her a mixed recent profile; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 44 days off and a 128 lb burden are tests of whether that winning fitness has been maintained.

runners_data.name: Bellesque
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's second string leads alongside a stablemate in what is a congested pace scenario; her three recent runs on Good ground (1W, 3P) show admirable consistency but her OR of only 92 against rivals rated up to 120 is a significant class deficit, and Declan McDonogh may find she is outgunned once the pace begins to tell after halfway.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out after winning two starts back, Bellesque arrives on a fair fitness gap of 22 days with experience of today's trip and going in her favour, and carries 128 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Damsel In Distress
runners_data.note: Daniel McLoughlin filly with a win over 8f on Good in her recent form — a relevant credential for this trip — and Ben Coen keeps the ride; her prominent style suits a strongly-run race if she can find a position just behind the scrapping leaders, though her trainer's 0/19 strike rate over 14 days adds a small note of caution around current yard form.|
runners_data.comment: Damsel In Distress arrives here in fine fettle just 15 days on from a winning effort, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; a fourth last time out is the only blemish, and at 128 lb our top-rated runner looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Exceptionally
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien runner rated 120 but showing three consecutive placed efforts without winning — the 0W/2P record on similar going flags a horse that competes without converting; Wayne Lordan will likely push for the early lead, but with Ballyskeagh and Bellesque equally committed, Exceptionally may end up in a costly pace battle that benefits the midfield runners she is meant to keep honest.|
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last three starts, Exceptionally arrives here in good order on 20 days' rest and has run over today's trip and going before, but she remains yet to win in recent starts and her rating of 90 leaves her mid-pack against this field.

runners_data.name: Samnina
runners_data.note: Shane Foley and Mrs John Harrington combine with a filly rated 120 who won over 7f last time and steps up to a mile; her OR and proven ability to win are the key credentials here, and her prominent style means she should sit just off the pace battle without being embroiled in it — 32 days since last run is manageable and her two-from-two record on Good going is exactly the form basis a prominent tracker needs.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a modest speed rating of 77, Samnina is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, and at least comes here fresh from stall two.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Rain
runners_data.note: Bolger-trained filly with the most extensive recent form in the field — six runs, 1W and 4P on Good — and Colin Keane takes the mount; she is a natural prominent racer but with four horses ahead of her competing for those positions, she is likely to find herself racing further back than ideal, and a style fit score of 0.92 confirms her chance must be tempered in a shape where she cannot get her natural berth.|
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Rain brings strong claims on the back of a win two starts back and a sequence of placed efforts in recent starts, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the fourth last time out is the one blemish to address.

runners_data.name: So Lovely
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners the Aidan O'Brien filly rated 120 with three consecutive placed or winning efforts on Good ground, including a win last time out — the combination of top jockey, powerful yard, highest-quality form and a prominent style that suits a truly-run race makes this a compelling profile; 9 days since last run is fresh but Moore will manage that, and she is the horse most likely to travel menacingly through the pace and sprint clear.|
runners_data.comment: So Lovely arrives in cracking nick, a winner last time out and placed in each of her two starts before that, and she has experience of both today's trip and the going; the chief concern is whether 128 lb from stall seven will blunt that momentum.

runners_data.name: Speckles
runners_data.note: Second Aidan O'Brien runner in the field, rated 120 but with only a placed effort and a sixth in two runs — Ronan Whelan takes the mount rather than Moore, which tells its own story about pecking order within the yard; her prominent style suits the race shape but her limited form makes it hard to identify her as a likely winner even if the scenario unfolds perfectly for a prominent tracker.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts, with a sixth two starts back undermining confidence, Speckles faces a stiff task on these figures, though a return to a familiar trip and a run just 20 days ago at least leaves her fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Sword Of State
runners_data.note: Brendan Duke's hold-up runner, a genuine closer at the back of the field, who must produce a career-best to feature at this level — she has a win on her record but also an eighth and a seventh, and Rory Cleary needs significant gaps to open in a compressed field; the OR of only 78 against rivals rated up to 120 makes this a very stiff ask even in the ideal late-running scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Sword Of State won one start back but has since finished eighth, and with a speed rating of just 59 she ranks eighth of ten on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going and returning quickly enough on an 11-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Tosca No Candis
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar filly who drops back in trip slightly having struggled over 8f on Good in her last two runs but won over 6f on Standard ground; her hold-up style means she needs the pace to fully implode and a clear run to finish, and W J Lee must thread through a crowded field — the zero wins and zero places from three runs on Good going specifically is a form concern that cannot be overlooked.|
runners_data.comment: Tosca No Candis arrives on the back of a win last time out and gets in from stall one carrying 128 lb, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the risk is that three of her four recent starts ended in fifth.

races.paceDynamic: Exceptionally, Ballyskeagh and Bellesque are three confirmed front-runners in a ten-runner field, and with all three likely to press for the lead from the outset, a strong, unrelenting gallop from flag to finish is virtually guaranteed over this flat Curragh mile on Good ground. The early stages will see a genuine battle for supremacy up front, burning through energy reserves and placing a premium on stamina and the ability to sustain effort into the final two furlongs. Prominent runners Samnina, Damsel In Distress, So Lovely and Speckles will be scrapping for the next tier of positions two to three lengths off the pace, creating a compressed and potentially congested mid-race scenario between the two-furlong and three-furlong poles that introduces real traffic risk for horses attempting to improve through. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel smoothly in midfield or just off the pace and unleash a sustained late run once the front three have burnt each other off — the ideal profile here is a horse with class, a clean passage and genuine stamina for a truly-run mile. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can physically all hold their desired positions; among the three confirmed leaders, Ballyskeagh (OR=120, recent winning form) and Exceptionally (Aidan O'Brien, consistent placer) are most likely to actually secure positions at or very near the head of affairs, with Bellesque perhaps slotting in just behind despite her front-running inclination.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out by halfway, leaving midfield stalkers to sweep past the exhausted leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The relentless early pace set by Exceptionally, Ballyskeagh and Bellesque will turn this into a true stamina test, and horses who have covered the ground efficiently from the second rank will find themselves with rivals stopping in front of them entering the final furlong; So Lovely's consistent placed form over this trip and Samnina's recent winning run both suit this shape precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Ballyskeagh — finds a superior cruising speed and opens a decisive gap by the three-furlong pole, making the race a test of who can run them down.
scenarios.body: Ballyskeagh's OR of 120 and recent course-and-distance winning form give her the class to dictate without being destroyed by the pace battle, and if she gets a clean, uncontested lead early while Exceptionally and Bellesque fight each other, she could hit the rising ground in front and sustain all the way to the line; a horse of this profile winning a truly-run race from the front requires rare class, and her rating and form suggest she possesses it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Hold-Up Scores
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group becomes hopelessly bunched between two and three furlongs out, blocking those travelling just behind and giving a hold-up runner a gap along the rail or outer late.
scenarios.body: Sword Of State and Tosca No Candis are the genuine hold-up types in this field, and if the prominent congestion materialises and creates a gap in the dying strides, a horse finishing strongly from the rear could ambush a tiring field; the concern is that neither hold-up runner carries strong enough form credentials — Sword Of State's inconsistency and Tosca No Candis's limited form in similar company temper expectations even in their optimal shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Grinds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to destroy the three leaders but not quite brutal enough to fully reel them in, leaving a prominent tracker to grind out a narrow victory on the line.
scenarios.body: Damsel In Distress or Speckles, sitting just off the leaders and covered up early, could find themselves in an ideal tracking position if the pace is severe without being truly suicidal, allowing them to inherit the lead passing the two-furlong pole and hold on as the closers arrive just too late; this scenario requires a precise calibration of pace that is the least predictable outcome given three genuinely committed front-runners in opposition.

watchPoints.text: Ballyskeagh, Exceptionally and Bellesque will all seek the early lead — watch the first furlong for a three-way battle for supremacy that could set a suicidally fast pace and dramatically compromise all three of their finishing chances.

So Lovely is the horse most likely to benefit from the pace scenario: watch Ryan Moore positioning her two lengths off the scrapping leaders in the first half-mile, as a clean passage for her in the straight could be decisive.

The prominent group of Samnina, Damsel In Distress, Speckles and Sea Of Rain will be compressed in a two-to-four-length band between two and three furlongs out — watch for severe traffic trouble as this group tries to quicken simultaneously through a narrowing gap.

Sea Of Rain's redistribution to midfield means Colin Keane must ride a waiting race entirely out of her natural style — watch whether she can adapt or whether racing out of role costs her momentum at the critical point when the race heats up approaching the two-furlong pole.

Sword Of State and Tosca No Candis as genuine hold-up runners will need an unusually severe pace collapse to get involved — watch the clock at halfway to gauge whether the front-runners have truly set a lung-bursting gallop that leaves those two with a realistic late chance.

races.name: Audi Naas Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by Donnacha Aidan O'Brien whose recent form (three places from five Good-ground runs) suggests consistent but not dominant ability; stepping up to 7f for the first time is an unknown, and sharing lead duties with two others at OR=85 makes this a high-energy assignment for a 3lb-claiming jockey.
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile with thirds two and three starts back, and a second four starts back, Tradewinds steps up with experience over today's trip and going, fit enough on 20 days' rest; yet to score in recent starts, but our rating of 93 marks him as one to take seriously from stall one.

runners_data.name: Banks Of The Boyne
runners_data.note: Most compelling form in the field having won over this exact 7f Curragh trip 9 days ago at OR=79; Michael Mulvany's runner is fresh, course-proven, and if it can clear the early pace battle it has the strongest recent evidence of seeing out this distance on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Banks Of The Boyne arrives on the back of a win last time out and looks to have strong claims returning nine days later in fine form, having already encountered today's distance and going; the main risk is whether 137 lb blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Luca Brillante
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's hold-up runner has shown ability over 8f on Good ground, finishing second last time, and drops back to 7f here which may sharpen its finishing effort; Chris Hayes provides stable experience and this horse is structurally well-placed to benefit from the anticipated pace war without needing to make its own early running.
runners_data.comment: Luca Brillante ran a solid second last time out and returns in good order after just 11 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour; the worry is that she remains winless in recent starts and must prove she can go one better.

runners_data.name: Margot Mae
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this confirmed front-runner for Mrs John Harrington, who has not run for 51 days — the longest layoff in the field — which introduces a fitness query heading into a likely pace battle; has not placed on Good going in its two attempts on that surface and faces three rivals fighting for the same front position.
runners_data.comment: Margot Mae shaped well when third two starts back and our rating has her marginally top of these rivals, but she has been winless in recent starts and 51 days off the track is a fitness query she must answer here.

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's hold-up runner is flagged as one that fades in the finish, which is a serious concern in a race expected to have a strong early pace that will demand a genuine late kick; three runs, zero places, all on Good ground — the evidence does not suggest this shape will unlock improvement, and the tongue-tie has not yet produced a breakthrough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of tail-end finishes his most recent efforts, Elyatta is hard to fancy on these figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; he carries 121 lb from stall five, and our rating of 75 leaves him well held among these.

runners_data.name: Exchange Student
runners_data.note: J A Stack's runner holds the lowest rating in the field at OR=55 and is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is unlikely to be reproduced here given the field's rear-heavy makeup; four runs without a place on Good ground and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.90 signal that racing out of role in a fast-tempo race compounds an already difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Exchange Student heads into this rated just 55 officially and ranked last on our figures, making her hard to fancy; she does have experience over today's trip and going, and 24 days since her last run leaves her reasonably fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Tradewinds, Banks Of The Boyne, and Margot Mae are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field, meaning a strong, unrelenting gallop is virtually guaranteed from the outset over this flat Curragh 7f. With three pace-setters fighting for the same real estate in the first two furlongs, there will be early pressure and potential scrimmaging for the lead, ensuring the pace remains honest throughout and stamina will be tested in the final two furlongs. Luca Brillante and Elyatta, the genuine hold-up types, will have cover handed to them and can settle off the strong early fractions, which structurally favours hold-up or late-running profiles — provided those horses have the class and finishing kick to close on a genuinely hot pace. Exchange Student is a true hold-up runner who has been mapped to midfield because this field carries more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate at the back; Banks Of The Boyne and Tradewinds are most likely to actually secure the positions at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Tradewinds, Banks Of The Boyne, and Margot Mae produces a genuinely strong early gallop that leaves them all vulnerable entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The constant early pressure will drain the front-runners' reserves, opening the door for horses settling off the pace to pick them off close home; this is the dominant shape given the structural mismatch of three confirmed leaders in a small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If Banks Of The Boyne, the most recent winner over course and distance, bounces quickly out and sets a controlled pace while the other front-runners fail to match strides early.
scenarios.body: Without a true pace war developing, Banks Of The Boyne can dictate from the front at a more manageable tempo and use its superior recent form to last home; the 7f on Good ground suits its profile and it has already won over this exact trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns so fiercely that every hold-up runner has the opportunity to swoop in the final furlong on a completely spent front group.
scenarios.body: Luca Brillante under Chris Hayes for D K Weld would be the principal beneficiary, having shown ability to finish well over a staying trip on Good ground; Elyatta would need to dramatically improve on three uninspiring efforts and its fade-in-finish flag makes it a vulnerable participant even in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders collectively slow midrace after burning each other out in the opening furlongs, allowing a prominent racer to time a run from the pack.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape as the sheer number of pace horses makes a mid-race lull improbable, and no runner in the field has a strongly established prominent-but-not-leading profile to exploit it cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Watch for early crowding involving Tradewinds, Banks Of The Boyne, and Margot Mae in the first two furlongs — three front-runners in a six-horse field create a meaningful risk of interference or a pace that collapses one of them before halfway.

Margot Mae's 51-day absence combined with its confirmed front-running style means it may be used up early without peak fitness, watch for it dropping out rapidly once the pace bites in the final two furlongs.

Elyatta is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and has finished 8th, 9th, and 10th in its three runs — watch for it to be a non-factor from the two-furlong pole even in a shape that nominally suits hold-up runners.

Luca Brillante is stepping down from 8f to 7f under Chris Hayes for D K Weld — watch whether it can switch off early behind the pace battle rather than getting drawn into racing more prominently than its style demands.

Exchange Student's redistribution to midfield means punters should watch whether it actually settles further back than its mapped position — if it is forced to race closer than its natural style, its chance deteriorates further beyond the STYLE_FIT discount already applied.

races.name: Heider Family Stables Round Tower Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Great Barrier Reef
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts, all at 6f on Good or Soft, with Ryan Moore booked for O'Brien's yard — the 74-day absence is the only query, but the form is progressive and this horse is ideally suited to sitting prominent off a single leader and unleashing a finish.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in a row make Great Barrier Reef a compelling threat, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the main concern is a 74-day absence since that last victory, with 136 lb to shoulder from stall five.

runners_data.name: Push The Boat Out
runners_data.note: Won impressively on debut over 6f Good just 20 days ago for a trainer firing at 1/11 over the past fortnight — a single run makes form assessment harder but the profile is highly relevant, and a naturally prominent style suits this expected race shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Push The Boat Out won last time out but ranks sixth of seven on our figures, with a speed rating of 75 doing little to inspire confidence at this level; he has run over today's trip and returns after 20 days, yet the weight of evidence makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Control
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, rated OR 100, with downward form (5-4-1 reading oldest to latest) suggesting they won at 5f but have regressed; stepping back to 6f from 7f is logical, but this horse's recent efforts at this trip have been modest and sustaining a controlled lead into the straight is needed for a big run.
runners_data.comment: Ruler's Control won three starts back and has since finished fourth and fifth, so he arrives here needing to recapture that form; experience over today's trip and going is in his favour, and he carries a workable 131 lb from stall one, but the five-week absence is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse (OR 99) whose four-run form includes two wins over 5f on Good, but the most recent effort was a fourth at 6f Good — the controlled pace set by a lone front-runner is a structural disadvantage, and Soumillon will need the race to fall apart late for this to land.
runners_data.comment: Where Love Lives won on each of his last two winning starts — victories three and four starts back — and arrives here fit enough on 30 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the concern is that he has finished outside the places in his two most recent outings.

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's filly has won over this 6f Good combination before and arrives on a 15-day turnaround — her natural instinct is to race prominently, but with the forward positions already filled, she is pushed back in this race shape and her chance is tempered by racing out of her preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Placed third on two of her last four starts and a winner four starts back, Beibhinn has experience of today's trip and going in her favour, though that sixth last time out and a mid-division draw 6 suggest she faces a stiff task off 128 lb against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 6f Good give this Colin Keane-ridden filly strong course and distance form, and she is arguably the most proven at this level among the displaced types — naturally wants to be prominent, but with Great Barrier Reef and Push The Boat Out ahead of her in the queue, she is unlikely to secure that ground and her chance diminishes as a result.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Livenka faces a stiff ask off 128 lb, and a 17-lb gap between her official mark and our rating is a real concern; in her favour, she has winning form in her last four starts and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Trained by P Twomey (0 from 14 over 14 days), OR 108, but the recent form string of 4-8-3-3-1 shows declining consistency over this trip and surface — a prominent type who has solid claims on ratings but needs the race to play out very specifically given modest recent 6f turf returns.
runners_data.comment: Velozee arrives here in sound shape just 20 days after her latest third, has experience of today's trip and going, and with two wins in her last six starts she carries plenty of class into this; the 128 lb burden is the one query, but on a rating of 111 she heads these rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Ruler's Control is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine rival willing to take them on for the lead — creating a scenario where they can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over six furlongs on Good ground at the Curragh. Push The Boat Out, Great Barrier Reef, and Velozee are all natural prominent types who will press close behind but lack the inclination to seize the lead themselves, meaning Ruler's Control sets the terms unchallenged. Livenka and Beibhinn are genuine prominent/press types but the field is too congested ahead of them — both are redistributed to midfield on the map despite their natural forward tendency, and it is Great Barrier Reef and Push The Boat Out who are best positioned to actually secure the prominent slots. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers tracking a lone, unhurried leader — horses who can sit just off a steady tempo and unleash a decisive finish will be most advantaged, with true hold-up horses like Where Love Lives dependent on a strong pace that this setup is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler's Control dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the race is decided by those tracking closest.
scenarios.body: Ruler's Control sets a sustainable rhythm through the early and middle stages, leaving the prominent horses — particularly Great Barrier Reef and Push The Boat Out — perfectly poised to sweep past in the final furlong as the leader tires. This shape rewards horses with tactical speed and a clean run from a prominent position, both of which Great Barrier Reef and Push The Boat Out possess in abundance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that Ruler's Control is never truly pressured and sustains the lead all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to apply pressure, Ruler's Control produces a front-running display at a tempo comfortable enough to maintain throughout, as rivals find themselves caught in a slow-motion tactical race before having to quicken from further back. This scenario rewards the leader directly and punishes hold-up types like Where Love Lives most severely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced prominent types — Livenka and Beibhinn — push forward early and create a more contested pace than anticipated.
scenarios.body: Should Livenka or Beibhinn attempt to claim their natural position despite the crowded forward area, the early tempo quickens and the race becomes more of a true test of speed and stamina, opening the door for horses with a high cruising speed to sustain their effort. Push The Boat Out's strong recent form and Livenka's back-to-back wins make them the most likely beneficiaries if the pace genuinely increases.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong early pace develops and Where Love Lives is delivered late on a well-timed run.
scenarios.body: This shape requires a genuine pace collapse from the front to create the ground for a hold-up horse to close, and Where Love Lives — a confirmed hold-up type — would need everything to go wrong for the leaders simultaneously. Given the single, uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo, this is the least likely outcome, but Soumillon's tactical intelligence keeps a small chance alive if the front collapses dramatically in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Livenka or Beibhinn attempt to push forward at the start — if either commits to claiming a prominent position, the early tempo will quicken significantly and transform the race shape away from the controlled-pace scenario.

Ruler's Control sets the pace for all seven runners — if they are allowed to coast along unchallenged at a very slow tempo, the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole and raw speed ratings (favouring Push The Boat Out and Great Barrier Reef) will matter most.

Great Barrier Reef returns after 74 days off — Ryan Moore will likely be instructed to travel prominently, but any ring rustiness or failure to travel fluently in the early stages could leave this horse vulnerable to fresher rivals in the final furlong.

Where Love Lives will be last or near last for most of the race — monitor whether Soumillon makes his challenge wide in the straight or tries to thread through; in a small, seven-runner field on Good ground there is no structural reason to expect the pace to collapse enough for a hold-up horse to land.

races.name: Snow Fairy Fillies Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Bosphorus Rose
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with six runs on similar Good ground showing solid consistency (3W5P); W J Lee partners her off a short 15-day turnaround for P Twomey, and she handles this trip well — an each-way danger if she can slot into a clean position behind the pace.
runners_data.comment: Bosphorus Rose won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing she can mix it at this level, but a fifth last time out gives pause; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 133 lb from stall nine, and returns after a brisk 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Faiyum
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount is one of two genuine front-runners and will press for the lead from the gate; returns from a 116-day break which is a notable query, but her OR of 107 makes her the class leader up front and she's 3W2P on Good going — will set the standard for others to aim at.
runners_data.comment: Faiyum won three starts back and was third two starts back, showing consistent recent form, and she has distance and going experience to call on; the concern is a 116-day absence carrying 133 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: Older mare operating off a long losing run (-72500 form) and her recent profile is over shorter 7-8f trips rather than this 1m1f; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race but her form line gives little confidence at this level, and the headgear (tongue tie) suggests connections are searching.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Princess Child nonetheless brings strong distance and going experience to the table and her rating of 112 makes her a live threat in a field of 15; the risk is that her two most recent efforts were unplaced.

runners_data.name: Sindria
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Joseph O'Brien whose two wins have both come over 10f on Good or Soft — the trip is right; returning after 62 days and her form (11935) has dipped, but a strongly-run race is exactly the shape she needs and Declan McDonogh rides.
runners_data.comment: Sindria showed smart form with back-to-back wins four and five starts back, and experience over today's trip and going underlines her claims under 133 lb from stall five; the main concern is that she was beaten into fifth last time out after a 62-day absence.

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: In-form at her best with a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is 3/13, but her recent Good-ground profile is disappointing (0W0P across 11 comparable runs); this is a genuine hold-up mare who will be further back than ideal given the field configuration — the style fit discount is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Spicy Margarita nevertheless holds a rating edge over her official mark and has experience of today's trip and conditions, though a fourth is her best recent effort and she carries 133 lb from stall two after a 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides a horse with p-headgear who has been placed on Good going but never won on it across 12 comparable runs (0W2P); hold-up style suits a fast pace but she needs things to go right in running and the Curragh's galloping track requires a bigger engine than she may possess.
runners_data.comment: Syzygy shaped with promise when a second three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going, but winless in her last six starts and that ninth last time out raises questions she must answer from stall 10 carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Thalara
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's mare has been off 343 days — the longest absence in the field — but her last two Curragh runs on Good were a win and a third over this trip and course; prominent style and proven course-and-distance form make her interesting if the layoff hasn't blunted her, and Andrew Slattery gets the ride.
runners_data.comment: Thalara was a winner two starts back and has placed on three other recent occasions, but she returns from a 343-day absence and an unplaced effort last time gives her something to prove; she has run over today's distance and going before and carries 133 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Della Pace
runners_data.note: George Boughey's 3-year-old has run consistently around Good ground (3/8) with four consecutive top-four finishes over 10f; a natural hold-up type who will be racing further back than natural because of the field composition — that complicates her chance, though her trip form is solid.

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes a hold-up filly for A P O'Brien who won on Good-to-Soft but has recorded 0W1P on comparable Good going across five runs; the headgear (tongue tie) is noted — Moore's positional intelligence is the key asset if pace is strong enough to bring her into it late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 15 on our figures, Drop Dead Gorgeous has shaped poorly in her last three starts, finishing eighth, fifth, and ninth, and the return after 45 days adds an element of doubt; a win five starts back and experience over today's trip and going are slim comfort.

runners_data.name: Garden Party
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner for A P O'Brien and Wayne Lordan, she has won on Good going over this trip and brings upwardly mobile 3-year-old form (22-1); she will dispute the early pace with Faiyum and her presence ensures the gallop is genuine — her raw OR of 87 limits her claims once the race develops.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures with a speed rating of 66, Garden Party faces a stiff ask here, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out, has experience of today's going, and is fit enough on a 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan's 3-year-old arrives with four wins from her last five starts including two on Good going, and her prominent style means she can sit just off the pace without burning unnecessary energy; Chris Hayes has the experience to find a clean position in a congested field, and she looks the standout prominent profile.
runners_data.comment: Meriden arrives on the back of fine recent form, winning five of her last six starts and finishing second last time out, with experience over today's distance and going in her favour; 126 lb and stall 13 are the questions she must answer.

runners_data.name: Miss Scott
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon rides a Gosden-trained filly with 1W2P on Good going and a consistent recent record at 9-10f; her prominent style should allow her to travel into the race smoothly just off the pace, and the class of trainer and jockey combination adds confidence she will find a clean run in traffic.
runners_data.comment: Consistent filly who has won twice and finished second twice in her last four starts, and she has run over today's trip before; 126 lb from stall 15 and a rating of 102 place her mid-pack on paper, though her recent reliability makes her one to respect.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners a prominent-type 3-year-old who won on Soft last time; her Good-ground form shows 1W2P across eight runs but she was beaten by a long way in her two Curragh Good-ground appearances — the course profile is a mild concern despite the recent form uptick.
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Attack arrives on the back of a win last time out, and her experience over today's trip and going is an asset; she returns after 30 days off in sound shape and looks capable of going well from stall four off 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Saga Gaga
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner for M D O'Callaghan with two wins on Good over 10-12f, she has the right profile for this race shape but is likely to find herself further back than natural given the prominent congestion — Seamie Heffernan will need to be aggressive early or accept a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, Saga Gaga is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back; a fifth last time out and a lowly speed rating make her tough to recommend, though she has distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Sky Watch
runners_data.note: Another O'Callaghan runner with p-headgear and a record of 0W0P on comparable Good going across five runs; prominent by nature but her form here suggests she tends to find one or two too good at the finish — best watched to see if the headgear sharpens her response in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Sky Watch has placed third twice in her last two starts but ranks 14th of 15 on our figures, making her very hard to fancy against this field; she has run over today's trip and going before, and her win in her last five starts shows she can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Faiyum and Garden Party are the two confirmed pace-setters in a 15-runner field, and both are expected to stride forward from the gate, creating an honest, genuine gallop over 1m1f on Good ground at the Curragh. Behind them, a significant cluster of prominent-minded runners — Bosphorus Rose, Thalara, Meriden, Miss Scott, Pivotal Attack, and Sky Watch — will be competing for the next rank of positions, generating pressure from the second rank and compressing the midfield through the early and middle stages. The prominent position is oversubscribed: Saga Gaga is a natural prominent type who is likely to find herself shuffled into midfield, while Spicy Margarita and Della Pace are genuine hold-up horses who will also be operating further back than ideal, meaning the true closers are a thinner group than the map suggests. With a true pace on from the front and congestion in the prominent ranks, this race shape most favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first three or four off the pace — relaxed prominent-to-midfield types with a clean line of running and a turn of foot on Good ground — over those who need to deliver from the rear through a compressed, shuffled field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Faiyum and Garden Party set a genuine gallop and the race is run at an even tempo throughout, allowing a stalker to travel into the race.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners ensure the pace is genuine but not suicidal, setting up a race where the horse travelling best just off the pace has the energy to quicken decisively into the straight; the Curragh's flat, galloping track rewards horses who can sustain their run rather than needing a manufactured injection of pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Faiyum or Garden Party gains a soft lead and the field fails to apply pressure from behind, allowing a soft gallop that suits the front-runner.
scenarios.body: A contested early break between the two leaders settles into one dictating from the front at a deceptively comfortable pace as the prominent group checks and steadies; the leader finds themselves with reserves in the tank turning for home and holds on against late challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the contested lead burns genuinely hard fractions and the prominent cluster gets involved in the scrimmage, opening the race up for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: The burning pace from Faiyum and Garden Party, combined with the prominent congestion pulling those runners into the race too early, leaves the straight open to a horse who has conserved energy in midfield; a true hold-up runner who finds a gap late becomes dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Chaos Result
scenarios.trigger: If the overloaded prominent tier causes interference or blocking moves 2-3f out, disrupting the race for multiple fancied runners.
scenarios.body: The six-horse scramble for the prominent positions creates checking, angling-out and lost momentum at a critical stage, producing a messy finish where a horse with a wide draw or decisive jockey who avoids trouble emerges; runners on the outside of the field or with the most experienced jockeys in traffic benefit disproportionately.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Meriden, Miss Scott, Thalara, Pivotal Attack, Bosphorus Rose, and Sky Watch are all racing for the same positions 2-3f out; watch for bumping, checking, and lost momentum on the turn into the straight which could derail fancied runners.

Faiyum's 116-day absence is the longest layoff among front-runners — watch whether Colin Keane has to drive her hard from the gate to hold Garden Party, which could compromise her stamina in the final furlong and trigger an earlier collapse than anticipated.

Saga Gaga is a natural prominent racer who is likely to be shuffled into midfield by field dynamics — watch whether Seamie Heffernan goes forward aggressively early or accepts the compromised position, as the decision will shape the result for this filly significantly.

Thalara returns from 343 days off the track — watch her behaviour in the parade ring and in the early stages; if she travels strongly and settles, the layoff may be irrelevant given her proven Curragh Good-ground form, but any sign of greenness or sluggishness is telling.

Garden Party's draw and early position relative to Faiyum will determine whether they race genuinely against each other or one defers — if Garden Party slots behind Faiyum rather than pressing, the pace could be softer than anticipated and the race shape shifts toward Scenario B.

races.name: Tote Irish Cambridgeshire

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old operating at 5-7f almost exclusively in recent form, so stepping to a mile on a big track is a genuine query; hold-up style with Sam Coen's 5lb claim helps the weight, but distance looks the primary concern.
runners_data.comment: Big Gossey shaped well when second two starts back and has won twice in his last six starts, arriving fresh on 20 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the 142 lb burden is worth noting, but he heads the ratings as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Hardy Warrior
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old has placed in five of nine starts but has been running over 10f recently, and dropping back to a mile may sharpen the finish; hold-up style on a track where pace is modest is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Hardy Warrior shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out and was a winner five starts back, bringing strong recent form into this having run over today's trip and going; the main risk is that he has not recaptured that winning thread in his last four outings.

runners_data.name: Ribee
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form over 8f on heavy ground last time; Ben Coen rides and the prominent style suits, but the sim-going record at 0/5 on good turf is a real flag in these conditions today.
runners_data.comment: Ribee showed his best when scoring five starts back, and that winning form combined with experience over today's trip and going keeps him very much in the picture from stall six off 133 lb; the worry is he has finished fifth or worse in three of his four most recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has placed twice over 8f on good but the recent form string of 9-8-15-6-0 is not encouraging; hold-up style and a modest sim-going conversion rate make him a non-threatening outsider.
runners_data.comment: Rahmi shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, has experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 102 puts him firmly in contention from stall four on a return 22 days later; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 3% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's four-year-old has gone 7/7 on good going and won last time over this trip, so both surface and distance are fully proven; sits just off the pace and should have a clean view from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Pierre Royal won three starts back and was second two starts back, so he arrives in decent nick after 27 days off; he has run over today's trip and going before and carries 128 lb from stall 10, though a fourth last time out and a rating of 93 suggest he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher at 7-9f but has been beaten into mid-pack on every sim-going comparable run (0/15 places) and has not shown the ability to win in this type of competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lord Massusus at least returns on a manageable 27-day break with experience over today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 98 gives him fair claims from stall 11, though the 127 lb burden is a stern ask against this field.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner — won his last two starts at 8f on good ground and is trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery who will know exactly how to exploit an uncontested lead; 44 days off but form is rock-solid at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Loughrea arrives in cracking recent form — a winner last time out and two starts back, though he was only second three starts back and has had 44 days off the track since, which may blunt that sharpness slightly; experience over today's trip and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Dos Mukasan
runners_data.note: Recent form shows a tendency to fade late and the "fades in finish" flag is significant; his true back-of-the-field style has been pushed into midfield by redistribution, meaning he may neither get the cover he needs nor the clear run he requires — treat with caution.
runners_data.comment: Four consecutive starts without troubling the judge since winning five starts back make Dos Mukasan hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, and his speed figure of 75 underlines the concern; stall one and experience over today's trip are modest positives at best.

runners_data.name: Final Voyage
runners_data.note: Jessica Maye's 7lb claim takes the weight, and she rides a horse who handles good ground well — won over the trip earlier in the season; prone to inconsistency and the hold-up style is tricky on a day when the pace may not really run for closers.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out suggests Final Voyage is finding his feet again, but the trainer's dire recent strike-rate — just one winner from 29 — is a notable concern, and he has been inconsistent in recent starts, with only one win in his last six.

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: W.J. Lee takes the ride on a horse whose best form came when able to settle and deliver late; bumped into midfield by redistribution rather than running his natural hold-up race, which dilutes the chance in a shape where closers face a structural disadvantage today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Booyea faces a stiff ask from stall 16 carrying 124 lb, and an eighth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Hellorhighwater
runners_data.note: Four wins from four starts at 8f with the best two coming on good ground; Wayne Lordan booked from a 126-day break is the one flag to note, but the profile screams suitability for a Loughrea-led race where prominent trackers hold all the aces.
runners_data.comment: Hellorhighwater arrives in decent nick with back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, though 126 days off the track is a concern and his rating of 93 ranks him mid-pack in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last three runs show placed form over shorter and the mile on good ground suits well; redistributed into midfield because the rear is crowded, which slightly compromises his natural finishing pattern but David Marnane's yard is in form.
runners_data.comment: Manton Bay won last time out and returns quickly on eight days' rest, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; however, he finished eighth three starts back and is ranked towards the bottom of this field, so he faces a stiff ask from stall two off 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Kalir
runners_data.note: D.K. Weld's three-year-old has won two of his last three starts over this exact trip on good going and blinkers have sharpened him up; Chris Hayes takes over and the prominent style dovetails perfectly with the anticipated race shape.
runners_data.comment: Kalir won his last two outings so arrives in form, but our figures rank him well below the field here, and a speed rating of 71 makes him hard to fancy at the weights despite his recent back-to-back victories.

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Placed at 7f and 8f on good ground but also has runs of 11 and 15, making him unreliable; the prominent style is appropriate for the race shape but the overall form profile suggests a mid-division finish at best.
runners_data.comment: Playin Cool has shown he can mix it at this level, placing second and third in recent starts, but he is yet to win in his last five and returns after 51 days off, which adds a fitness query to his already inconsistent profile.

runners_data.name: Genuine Article
runners_data.note: Out-of-form with a sequence of 0-0-5 and a modest sim-going record; true hold-up type pushed further forward by redistribution than is ideal, and recent placings at 7-8f on good have been well beaten — hard to trust here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Genuine Article does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 27 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, his recent string of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy him strongly from stall 13 off 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but best recent efforts have come over 9-10f and today's mile may be on the sharp side; sim-going figures show only 2W3P in 15 comparable starts, suggesting the form in this precise context is limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, Slieve Binnian is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround in reasonable condition.

runners_data.name: Engines On
runners_data.note: Best form has come on soft ground (won on soft, placed on good-soft) and today's quicker surface is a concern; 76-day absence adds an unknown, and the prominent style suits the shape in theory but the ground fitness question looms large.
runners_data.comment: Engines On has been unplaced in each of his last three starts and, ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, is hard to fancy at this stage; he does at least return to a familiar distance and going, and that winning run four starts back is a reminder he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Has won twice over this exact trip on good ground and recently showed smart form at 8f; jockey Reese Holohan (7lb claim) is inexperienced at this level and the redistribution out of the deep hold-up berth he favours is a complication, though the raw ability is notable.
runners_data.comment: Johnny Soda has won three times in his last six starts, with a second last time out following back-to-back wins, so the recent form reads well enough, but he is ranked 14th of 18 on our figures and faces a stiff ask at the weights carrying 119 lb from stall 18.

races.paceDynamic: Loughrea is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field over a flat mile at the Curragh on good ground, and with no rival prepared to seriously contest the lead, Andrew Slattery's charge is set to control tempo from the front at whatever pace suits him — recent form of 1-1-2 at the trip underlines how well this role fits. Behind him, Hellorhighwater, Pierre Royal, Kalir, Ribee, Playin Cool, Slieve Binnian and Engines On will contest the prominent positions, creating a meaningful cluster of P-style horses chasing a solo leader, which should keep the early gallop honest without turning frantic. The redistribution caveat is important here: Dos Mukasan, Booyea, Manton Bay, Genuine Article and Johnny Soda are all genuine hold-up operators who cannot all find their natural position at the rear given the field size and the preponderance of hold-up types — those with the sharpest jockeys or widest draws are most likely to actually settle deep, while others will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Loughrea at a controlled tempo and deliver a sustained challenge over the final two furlongs, as true closers face the dual risk of a modest pace that never truly tests the leader and the traffic complications of an 18-runner mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loughrea Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Loughrea dictates a sustainable gallop and the P-style horses closest to him travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Loughrea sets fractions that suit himself while the prominent trackers get a clean run turning in, and the winner emerges from the group that has tracked the leader within three lengths. Kalir and Hellorhighwater profile ideally here — both have won at the trip on good ground and possess the cruising speed to collar a front-runner who has not been pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Loughrea Front to Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and no prominent rival lands a serious challenge until it is too late.
scenarios.body: Loughrea, having won back-to-back at this trip and course configuration, simply keeps rolling unchallenged and finds enough in the tank to hold every challenger off the home turn. With no natural pace rivals to force him off his rhythm, a solo front-runner on a 44-day freshener can prove very hard to peg back in a big field where rivals are stuck in traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Clears, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace develops an extra half-gear in the middle stages and genuine closers get a clear passage inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger-than-expected tempo from the prominent pack stretching to reach Loughrea opens a gap on the outside in the closing stages for a horse who has been patient. Johnny Soda — despite being redistributed — has shown real finishing speed over the mile on good ground and could benefit if Slattery finds a pocket of clear air late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types over-race early competing for positions behind Loughrea, causing a bunched, messy finish.
scenarios.body: Crowding among the P-style runners turns the race into a scramble approaching two furlongs out, with horses hanging left and gaps opening randomly. A horse like Booyea or Big Gossey, tucked in and presented with a gap, could plunge into the frame from an unexpected angle, though form figures make this a genuine outsider shot.

watchPoints.text: Loughrea — watch whether Andrew Slattery allows the pace to drift slow in the first half-mile; if unchallenged through 4f, the lack of a tempo-setter behind him makes him very hard to catch in the straight.

Hellorhighwater — 126 days off the track is a significant fitness query for a horse that Wayne Lordan is riding into a strongly-suited tactical scenario; if she has come back short of peak condition, the prominent position turns from asset to liability.

Kalir — watch the draw and early positioning: in an 18-runner mile at the Curragh, Chris Hayes must place him close enough to track Loughrea without getting squeezed by the pack of prominent rivals chasing the same ground.

Redistributed closers (Dos Mukasan, Booyea, Johnny Soda, Manton Bay) — monitor early in-running footage to see which of these genuinely settles back and which gets dragged into midfield by the crowd; those that secure their natural position will have a marginally better chance than the race-map implies.
Engines On — 76-day break and a ground preference for soft; if the track rides on the faster side of good, he could drop away quickly despite the prominent profile on paper.

races.name: Holden Plant Rentals Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for J G Coogan (0/2 T14) who has finished 7th, 13th, and 10th in three recent 6f Good runs — consistent form profile but no wins on sim going in 15 attempts; needs significant help from the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Andrew Slattery (3/22 T14) with a recent win on Good at 7f; stepping back to 6f is a valid query given her last five runs have all been at 7f or 8f, but she has early pace to burn and will contest the lead from the off.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but two unplaced efforts before that run and a tall weight of 141 lb from stall 18 give his supporters pause for thought.

runners_data.name: Naoi
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by style who drops back from a recent 7f Good win; Sam Coen's mount for W McCreery (3/18 T14) arrives on a short 9-day turnaround, and four placings from five runs on similar going suggest consistent quality — well-placed if the early leaders combust.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out — a win nine days ago on a quick turnaround — and she has run over today's trip and going before, which helps; however, that eighth two starts back is a concern, and ranked eighth of 21 here, she faces a stiff task carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type wearing a visor for Adrian McGuinness (4/24 T14); zero wins or places from six attempts on similar going and recent efforts have been modest — needs everything to fall perfectly in a big, competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Flaming rib is winless in his last five starts, yet our rating of 82 marks him out as the standout in a field of 21, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the risk is that his recent finishing positions — seventh and eighth in back-to-back outings — make the turnaround a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Poweracclaim
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for J P Murtagh (1/29 T14) whose best form at 6f Good includes two places; 49 days off the track is worth noting but his profile of tracking pace and finishing honestly suits this scenario well if he bounced back fit.
runners_data.comment: Poweracclaim caught the eye with a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating puts him comfortably clear of his official mark — a strong case for a big run; the main worry is 49 days off and a trainer firing at just 3% lately.

runners_data.name: Four Blondes
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Ross O'Sullivan (0/20 T14) on a quick 7-day turnaround; 13 of 15 similar-going runs have been on Good, zero wins but two places — moderate profile but course familiarity at 6f Good gives him a chance of sneaking into frame late.
runners_data.comment: Four Blondes has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 77 — ranking her third in a field of 21 — makes her a leading threat on a quick seven-day turnaround; the concern is a trainer who is yet to land a winner in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Gerard Keane returning after 56 days off; best two form figures have been at 5f rather than 6f (2nd and 10th), raising a genuine distance suitability question that compounds the hold-up style disadvantage in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lethimfly does at least hold experience over today's trip and going, and a second four starts back shows he can get competitive; however, three consecutive unplaced efforts since, plus 56 days off the track and a hefty 135 lb to carry, make improvement hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Call The Cavalry
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old for Chris Timmons (0/7 T14) all of whose recent form is on Flat/Standard — no comparable Good ground form to reference, making his projection particularly uncertain on this surface and in this competitive 21-runner scenario.
runners_data.comment: Call The Cavalry is winless in his last five starts, with his best recent effort a second four starts back, and an unplaced run last time out does little to inspire; experience over today's trip and a quick 14-day turnaround offer some encouragement, though his rating of 62 suggests he faces a stiff task from 21 runners.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking five-year-old for Charles Weld with a notably consistent record at 6f on Good (2nd, 2nd in recent runs); wears a hood, has 10 runs on similar going for 1W 3P, and Rory Mulligan's booking gives him solid tactical options in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Twice a runner-up in her last six starts yet winless in that spell, Rosato arrives on a quick seven-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, though carrying 132 lb from stall 16 on a modest official mark of 62 leaves her with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Adrian McGuinness (4/24 T14) who finished 2nd at 6f Good and 4th at the same course and conditions — three-year-old with nine runs on similar going for one place, making him an each-way live candidate if he secures a handy position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back and a third four starts back hint at ability, while experience over today's trip and going offers some comfort; the 131 lb burden from stall 10 looks the main obstacle to reversing recent fortunes.

runners_data.name: Top Biller
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed pace-setters for Denis Gerard Hogan (2/23 T14); has back-to-back runner-up finishes at 6f Good but has been off 72 days — fitness is a genuine concern, yet if sharp enough he will fight for the lead and could sustain better than Tawaazon or Faoladh.
runners_data.comment: Top Biller is winless in his last six starts, and a ranking of 19 from 21 on our figures makes him hard to fancy here; 72 days off adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the two seconds in recent starts offer some crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Apothic Red
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking three-year-old wearing a visor for T G McCourt (0/14 T14); best run on similar going was a 2nd at 6f Good, but five of seven sim-going runs have yielded just that one place — needs to improve.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Apothic Red at least shaped with some promise when second last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 128 lb from stall eight, he rates a shade better than his official mark of 61 suggests, though consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Solid recent form includes a 1st at 6f Good and a 2nd at 7f, and Ms Claire O'Connell's three-year-old has genuine hold-up ability — however, she is redistributed to midfield because this field carries too many true back-markers, meaning she will likely race slightly forward of her comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Dervo Annie showed her best when winning and finishing second in earlier starts, but a seventh and sixth in her last two runs suggest she's gone off the boil; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, though a mark of 61 and draw seven make her a tough each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old confirmed front-runner for John Andrew Kinsella wearing a tongue-strap; 13 of 15 sim-going runs have come on Good but recent efforts at 5f suggest the step to 6f is a query — will force the early pace but may find the distance tests his stamina against younger rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tawaazon heads here just six days after his latest fifth, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, a rating of 63 from stall six at 126 lb leaves him with plenty to find against a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Wears a hood, has a pattern of hold-up racing, but the sheer volume of closers in this field means he ends up mapped to midfield — Paul W Flynn's five-year-old has zero wins on sim going from 14 attempts, and his recent form (9th, 11th, 15th, 18th) is deeply uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three unplaced efforts sandwiching a ninth last time out, Caffu Zafeen is hard to fancy from stall 19 on a 5% trainer strike rate; he has run over today's trip and going, but little else in the profile compels.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Adrian McGuinness (4/24 T14) who won at 5f Good earlier in his career; recent form has been patchy (14th, 8th, 16th) and the 6f trip has produced modest efforts — needs to find significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: A winner six starts back, I'm Spartacus has been largely out of the cards since, finishing eighth two starts back and unplaced last time out just six days ago; the quick turnaround and a rating 13 points above his official mark offer some hope, but the recent form makes belief a stretch.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a 2nd at 5f Good on the form card; wears a hood, and his natural inclination to race from behind means he is positioned to midfield on the map — but he is racing out of his preferred role and his five-furlong best form may not fully translate to 6f under this pressure.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, Simmering Seas is hard to fancy despite her experience over today's trip and going; a second two starts back is the best she offers, and six days since her last run at least suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Strikepoint
runners_data.note: Three-year-old flagged as fading in the finish — a significant concern in a race with a hot pace; natural hold-up tendency mapped to midfield due to redistribution, limited form (3 runs), and a fade flag makes this a very difficult profile to be confident about here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a ninth last time out the chief concern, Strikepoint heads here 14 days later rated just 54 officially and ranked 17 of 21 on our figures; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 14-day turnaround, are slim pickings for optimism from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who placed 3rd at 7f Good but whose 6f form reads 8th and 15th; Eddie & Patrick Harty's runner is a genuine hold-up type nudged forward on the map, and the shorter trip combined with this role displacement makes for a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Fontaine Khaled makes this very difficult to fancy — winless in her last six starts, with a fifth last time out and only a solitary third three starts back to offer any encouragement, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns on a reasonable 22-day break.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Won at 5f Good earlier this season for Miss Jennifer Anne Lynch; wears a hood, and her natural position is at the rear — forced into midfield on the map in this packed field. The step to 6f is a query given all five recent runs were at 5f.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures and carrying 119 lb from stall 15, Another Nice'day faces a stiff ask, his sole win in his last six starts coming three runs back amid a largely inconsistent recent record, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-strap and is a hold-up horse for J G Coogan (0/2 T14) who has never run beyond 8f competitively at winning level; recent efforts have all been on Good but finishes of 6th, 12th, 6th suggest no form at this trip — wide on the map and out of role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Pure Valour faces a stiff task here; she does arrive on a sharp 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going to her name, but that is the limit of the encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh, Top Biller, and Tawaazon are all confirmed front-runners in a 21-horse, 6f handicap at the Curragh on Good ground, making a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset virtually certain. With three horses fighting for the early lead, the pace will be genuine and sustained — this is not a race where any one leader can dictate cheaply or control the tempo. That hot early pace on a flat 6f track in Good conditions sets up powerfully for horses who can race prominently without burning too much fuel, or sit just off the battle and pounce in the final furlong; pure hold-up horses face a meaningful disadvantage, however, because several of the field's truest hold-up types — Dervo Annie, Strikepoint, Simmering Seas, Caffu Zafeen, Fontaine Khaled, Another Nice'day, and Pure Valour — have been redistributed to midfield on the map as genuine hold-up horses unable to secure their natural rear position in this traffic-heavy scenario. The race shape firmly favours horses with a prominent or handy early position who can sustain their effort through the final two furlongs once the pace-battle takes its toll on the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle burns itself out in the first half and a prominent-tracking horse swoops at the two-furlong pole
scenarios.body: Faoladh, Top Biller, and Tawaazon fight vigorously for supremacy through the first three furlongs, creating a truly hot pace that leaves them vulnerable late; a horse sitting just off this battle in a prominent position — conserving energy while on the heels of the leaders — is ideally placed to capitalise as the leaders flatten out. Poweracclaim, Coincidental Glory, and Rosato all have the profile to track the pace without being drawn into the early war, and Good going suits their form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Sustain, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh or Top Biller establishes a fractionally cleaner lead and the pace, while strong, is more uniform than chaotic
scenarios.body: A single front-runner who clears the early scrimmage and finds a rhythm can be surprisingly hard to catch over 6f at the Curragh when the gallop is even rather than frantic; Faoladh's recent winning form at 7f on Good and Top Biller's two second-place finishes at 6f on Good both suggest these horses can sustain competitive effort the full trip. In this shape the leader who gets first run and best rail position holds on as the field fans wide behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wide Midfield Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so brutal that it creates a significant rebound and a horse from a genuine midfield position (not redistributed) closes with a powerful late run
scenarios.body: A truly scorching early pace can occasionally generate enough of a vacuum behind the leaders that a horse racing from mid-division, not genuinely at the rear, sweeps through beaten rivals in the final furlong; Naoi (form: 3338-1, recent 7f winner on Good, likely to sit off a strong pace) and Four Blondes (consistent 6f Good course form) are the most credible candidates whose natural style places them in that mid-division bracket without redistribution caveats. This scenario demands everything goes right in traffic for a 21-runner field and is conditional on the pace truly collapsing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the field is so chaotic that gaps appear late and a genuine hold-up horse threads through to win despite being forced forward
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the majority of true hold-up horses are redistributed to midfield and will already be racing out of role, diminishing their ability to produce the sustained late finish that closing scenarios demand; Dervo Annie (1W in 6f Good, STYLE_FIT=0.93) and Another Nice'day (won 5f Good, STYLE_FIT=0.91) are the most live of this group, but both face the compounding challenge of a full-field 21-runner race where traffic issues at the Curragh over 6f are severe. Discount this scenario significantly given how many natural hold-up types are already displaced forward.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh, Top Biller, and Tawaazon are all likely to fight aggressively for the early lead — watch for any one of them getting completely buried by the battle before the halfway mark, which would accelerate the burnout and dramatically open the door for prominent trackers.
